clue.text: Building by sea where piece is written by novelist

indicators.note: one piece is written beside the other, so the novelist's name comes first and the chess piece follows

parts.note: George Sand was the pen name of a nineteenth-century French novelist
a castle (rook) is a piece in chess

explanation.surface: A building at the seaside where a novelist sat writing a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' suggests writing, but it is a chess piece; 'is written by' puts the novelist's name first.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's beach structure moulded from damp grains is a small building by the sea.

clue.text: Fire rifle

definitions.meaning: to fire someone is to dismiss them
to rifle is to plunder

explanation.definitionFit: Dismissing an employee and plundering a town are both meanings of the word.

clue.text: Scores, for example, in book

definitions.meaning: a score is twenty, an example of a figure
the fourth book of the Old Testament

explanation.definitionFit: Twenties are figures, and the fourth book of the Bible bears this title.

clue.text: Date poet got for trial

parts.note: to date someone is to court them
Martial was a Roman poet famous for his epigrams

explanation.surface: A poet went out on a date and was put on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: MARTIAL is the Roman epigrammatist, a poet crosswords often use.
explanation.definitionFit: A military tribunal is a trial of service personnel.

clue.text: A little point put delicately

parts.note: S, for south, is a point of the compass
lightly means gently, delicately

explanation.surface: A small point made in a delicate, tactful way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a compass point, here S for south.
explanation.definitionFit: To a small degree, marginally.

clue.text: Artful place for a shutter

definitions.meaning: a place full of art, the great Paris gallery
a slatted shutter or vent

explanation.definitionFit: The Paris museum is a place full of art, and a slatted window cover shares its spelling.

clue.text: Everyone has been a follower of this style of architecture

definitions.text: Everyone has been a follower of this
definitions.meaning: in the biblical account all humans descend from the first man, so everyone has followed him
the neoclassical style of Robert ... and his brothers, eighteenth-century Scottish architects

explanation.definitionFit: Genesis makes the first man the ancestor everyone follows, and the Adam brothers gave their surname to a Georgian architectural style.

clue.text: Get little girl to sign records

parts.note: Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A girl is persuaded to sign some records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' looks like a verb but is a star sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Daily journals are personal records of events.

clue.text: Skilful treatment for bosses

definitions.meaning: skilful handling of a situation or person
the managers of a firm collectively

explanation.definitionFit: Handling something deftly, and the people in charge of a company, share the word.

clue.text: Stop dismissing a remarkable official statement

indicators.note: dismissing means the letter a is sent away from the punctuation word

parts.note: a comma is a punctuation mark, a stop in writing
unique means one of a kind, remarkable

explanation.surface: Someone tells a remarkable person to stop sending people away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing a' removes A from COMMA, leaving COMM.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal bulletin issued to the press by a government or body is a communiqué.

clue.text: Eve and she are far apart

definitions.text: Eve and she are far apart

parts.words: Eve and she are far apart
parts.note: read as two women's names it seems to be about two people, but eve is evening, and the other is the opposite end of the night, also a girl's name

explanation.surface: Two women, Eve and another, live far from each other.
explanation.walkthrough: Eve reads as a woman's name but means evening; the answer is the start of day, far from evening, and also a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Daybreak lies at the other end of the night from evening, and it is also a woman's first name.

clue.text: Playwright's including text showing Falstaff's failing

indicators.note: including means the playwright's name takes the text word inside it

parts.note: Noel Coward was an English playwright; with the 's
lines are the text an actor learns

explanation.surface: A playwright's script reveals the failing of Shakespeare's Falstaff.
explanation.walkthrough: Falstaff, Shakespeare's fat knight, is famously cowardly; 'including' puts LINES inside COWARD'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Falstaff runs from danger, so his flaw is a lack of courage.

clue.text: Defeat champion

definitions.meaning: to beat them
the top performer, the winner

explanation.definitionFit: To outdo an opponent is to beat them, and the finest competitor is the top one.

clue.text: Breaking new ground can be distressful

definitions.meaning: literally, breaking up soil with a farm harrow
deeply upsetting

explanation.definitionFit: A harrow is a farm tool that breaks up soil, and a harrowing experience is deeply upsetting.

clue.text: Candidate on trial is unable to get about

indicators.note: get about means the word for unable goes around the other pieces

parts.note: can't means unable
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A candidate on trial cannot get around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get about' puts CAN'T around ON + TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone competing for a prize or post is a candidate.

clue.text: Check outside broadcast to Newcastle

indicators.note: the first part of the city's name, new, tells us the remaining word castle is made new by rearranging

explanation.surface: An outside broadcast unit is sent to Newcastle to check something.
explanation.walkthrough: The city name Newcastle splits: 'New' is the anagram signal, and CASTLE is rearranged to STACLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hindrance or impediment is something that checks progress.

clue.text: Condition I'm following throughout

indicators.note: following places the word I'm after the condition word

parts.note: a pass is a state of affairs, as in 'things have come to a pretty pass'

explanation.surface: Someone says what condition they are following throughout.
explanation.walkthrough: PASS as a condition comes from the idiom 'come to a pretty pass'.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin used in footnotes to mean a term occurs everywhere in a text, all through it.

clue.text: Army's food not totally without flavour

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, the British reserve force, plus the 's
a table can mean the food served, as in 'keeps a good table'

explanation.surface: Army food is not completely flavourless.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve; 'table' as food is an old sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be tasted has at least some flavour.

clue.text: What radio-carbon's been used for until now

definitions.meaning: radiocarbon dating is used ... ancient things
as yet, so far

explanation.definitionFit: Carbon-14 is used for dating finds, and 'so far' is the everyday sense.

clue.text: Refuse to go through cases

definitions.meaning: to turn down
in grammar, to ... a noun is to give its case forms

explanation.definitionFit: Turning something down, and listing a noun's grammatical forms, are both meanings.

clue.text: No sailor's withdrawn from England's manoeuvre

indicators.note: the letters are drawn out of the run of words England's manoeuvre

explanation.surface: A sailor has been withdrawn from an English naval manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn from' takes the letters inside 'EngLAND'S MANoeuvre'.
explanation.definitionFit: A landsman is someone unfamiliar with the sea, a person who lives ashore.

clue.text: Not a man out of order in this state

indicators.note: out of order means the letters of not a man are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A man in this state is behaving out of order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' rearranges NOT A MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A large state in the north-western US, known as Big Sky Country.

clue.text: Cast off from island in part of Ireland

indicators.note: in puts the island abbreviation within the county name

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone casts off from an island in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is in Northern Ireland; 'in' puts IS inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate or reject someone, refusing any tie, is to cast them off.

clue.text: One who's not right is stoical when wrong

indicators.note: the words is stoical, when made wrong, are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone politically left stays calm and stoical even when proved wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when wrong' rearranges the letters of IS STOICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the political left is not of the right wing.

clue.text: Sounds like my property includes a Scottish island

indicators.note: the clue says the answer sounds like the phrase that follows

parts.note: if a is among my property, I own a

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that their estate includes a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my property includes a' becomes the spoken phrase 'I own a', which sounds like the island's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A small island of the Inner Hebrides, famous for its abbey founded by St Columba.

clue.text: Not a lot of liquid in sight

definitions.meaning: a small drop, as of sweat
the small front sight on a gun barrel

explanation.definitionFit: A tiny drop of moisture, and the knob on a gun barrel used for aiming, share the word.

clue.text: Hungry French artist lacking capital

indicators.note: capital means the first letter, so the painter's name loses its head

parts.note: Jacques-Louis David was a French neoclassical painter

explanation.surface: A hungry French painter has no money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money but means the capital (first) letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager, keen or greedy for something, as in avid for news.

clue.text: Delayed reaction as result of second helping?

definitions.meaning: a startled second look after a delay
taking a portion twice, a double serving

explanation.definitionFit: A delayed look of surprise is a double take, and taking food twice reads playfully as the same phrase.

clue.text: The leader from Moscow opposed to US

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, taken here from Moscow

explanation.surface: The Moscow leader sets himself against the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US' looks like the United States but is just 'us', the opposite of 'them'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the phrase 'us and them' the other side, those opposed to us, are the pronoun given.

clue.text: See where changing rooms may be?

definitions.meaning: to see is to grasp or comprehend
at a sports ground the changing rooms may be beneath the grandstand

explanation.definitionFit: To see a point is to grasp it, and dressing rooms at a ground often sit beneath the grandstand.
